evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: No framing present. Call opens with 'Let me just double-check one moment, okay, may I please have your email address?' — no time-box, no promise, no wait for a yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep jumps directly into confirming existing quote details and packing service clarification without asking for the customer's overall concerns or what they want answers to.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Two estimates given ($2,341 for 4-hour packing scenario, $2,700 with three movers) but no typical range for a 1-bedroom and no personalization tied to customer's specific situation beyond the packing variable. No 'this feels fair' framing.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Call ends with rep asking only 'Alright, thank you, thank you so much. Alright, bye.' — no explicit ask for the business, no booking taken, no confirmation of next steps beyond 'I'll leave a note on your profile.'

top_strength: Rep effectively managed a complex, multi-variable pricing scenario (packing hours, crew size, Friday vs. Thursday rates, 3 PM entry constraint) and offered sensible solutions like adding a third mover and requesting photo documentation.
coaching_note: This call never transitioned from inbound-quote-modification mode to a sales call — there was no opening frame, no agenda discovery, no estimate close, and no booking ask; treat callbacks on existing quotes as full sales opportunities, not just service adjustments.
